items.item:
- INV-026, INV-027, INV-028: the budget derivation check. INV-026: an
  accepted import stores the published planned values and rewrites no budget
  version, plan or expense; a changed re-publication is a conflict that
  changes no snapshot, budget version, plan or expense and is recorded only
  as its import result and audit (A12, A13); expense operations never move a
  plan. INV-027: no table
  has a derived-value column, reading the views writes nothing, and after
  each change of an owning record (inclusion, allocations, progress,
  payment, plan) the next read equals a recomputation from the stored rows.
  INV-028: no service code deletes or replaces a portal section and no store
  surface removes one; activating a budget version without an allocated
  section is refused and writes nothing, and the activation keeps the
  sections progress references
  [witness: verification:budget_derivation_client_portal].
statements: INV-026: planned budget values never derive from actual expenses; mutable PresuPro estimate state never changes the portal budget outside the snapshot import boundary
INV-027: budget totals and all financial aggregates are derived at read time, never stored as editable values
INV-028: a PortalSection referenced by any allocation or progress record is never deleted

items.item:
- INV-050: the budget derivation check: the project overview is equal for
  staff and viewer and on repeated reads, equal records inserted in either
  order (ties of sort order, dates and amounts) derive equal values, and the
  budget and payment views equal a recomputation from the owning records
  [witness: verification:budget_derivation_client_portal].
statements: INV-050: all derived values are deterministic and recomputable from owning records for the same accepted inputs

items.item:
- INV-044: the budget derivation check:
  `calculate_material_balance` and the budget view show an overspent section
  as a negative remaining, a section without a progress record reads
  completion `None` and completed work value `None`, and a project without a
  budget reads its views as not configured
  [witness: verification:budget_derivation_client_portal].
statements: INV-044: remaining materials show overspend as negative values, never clamped or hidden; missing data is presented explicitly, never replaced by zero unless zero is confirmed: a section without a progress record reads completion_percent None and completed_work_value None

quotes: witness.expect(not stored, f"table {table} stores derived columns {stored}")
witness.expect(not changed, f"reading the derived views wrote to {changed}")
witness.expect(got == want, f"{label}: section {section.display_name} reads {got}, records give {want}")
witness.expect(not deleting, f"service code deletes or replaces portal sections: {deleting}")
witness.expect(not removers, f"{surface.__name__} exposes section removal {removers}")
witness.expect(not changed, f"the refused activation wrote to {changed}")
verdicts.why: The check behaviorally asserts import immutability/conflicts, expense-plan separation, read-time recomputation after each named mutation, read purity, activation refusal with no writes, and preservation of sections/progress. However, the claims that no table stores any derived value and no service/store path can remove a section are only heuristic name/string/surface scans, so some violating implementations could escape detection.
